描述_ZN: The Heng Fang Stele was erected in the ninth month of the first year of the reign of Emperor Ling of the Eastern Han Dynasty (168). The topography is 223 cm in length and 107 cm in width. It is written in clerical script, with 23 lines and 36 characters. The monument is inscribed with the title "The monument of Heng Fujun, the former Wei Yuqing of the Han Dynasty", in 2 lines of 10 characters, with a vertical grid line between the two lines. The owner of the stele, Heng Fang, is Xingzu. He was an official to the rank of Yin of Jingzhao and a lieutenant of Bingbu, and had achievements in politics. His disciples and former officials, such as Zhu Deng, were engraved with stones to praise his merits. The last line of the inscription has two lines of small letters: "Mengsheng plain Leling Zhu Deng word Zhongxi book." The monument was originally in Shandong Wenshang Guojialou, the Qing Yongzheng eight years (1730) Wenshui flood decision, the monument sunken lying, by Guo Chengxi re-established. It now exists in the Bingling Gate of the Dai Temple in Tai'an, Shandong Province.　　The calligraphy of this stele is famous for its rich body and strong bones, and its simplicity and gravity. According to Yao Hua of the Qing Dynasty, the "Fetang Classical Manuscript", "Jingjun" is ancient, but the potential is very strict and neat, unlike the "Hengfang", which changes from strict to neat and out of the danger." He Shaoji commented that it is "stubborn in the square and ancient".　　This topography is the Qing topography of the National Palace Collection. The ink topography is excellent. The character "將" is less than half of the tablet, and the character "儀之" is already attached.　　This tablet was recorded in Zhao Mingcheng's "Jin Shi Lu" and Hong Shi's "Shu Shu" in the Song Dynasty, and Gu Yanwu's "Jin Shi Shu Ji" in the Qing Dynasty.
